title: THE RETURN-GIFT
author: CLAUDE

rounds.summary: The most intimate and unfamiliar rhythm after a district struggle and a generation ship: a child, a mother and a hospitable people across a closing seam. The Hollowfolk's law is neither a price nor a strawman; understanding it as a promise against abandonment changes the available gift and makes the seasonal handclasp possible. Illuminara's imperfect learning of the hearth-song is a concrete act of respect, while Pim, Tabitha and Yeshe all keep the right to refuse. The result is hopeful and bounded: the child returns safely without pretending her new kinship never happened.

First draft of S3 from C03, following B01. S3 starts after S2 CRITIC_CLOSE (T10, 2026-11-17T14:33Z). B01 biggest risk handled: Pim has her own voice and a decisive reading of the law (ha-ru = gift and come-back, so the gift goes both ways) and is never a bargaining token; the seam's small-tide mechanics (the Knock: a hand's width, a few breaths, four times a year) are planted by Yeshe in scene 2, matched to the family draught books in scene 3 and the Hollowfolk tally cord in scene 4 before they solve anything; Yeshe's objection (a promise is wind, a gift stays on the shelf) is answered by a reciprocal pair of gifts (a living seed jar that needs telling, a knotted cord with a knot per Knock) and a mother's pledge that the promise is Pim's to keep or refuse, not by instant agreement. R14 carriers: the decisive turn is understanding (the law was always a promise against abandonment; the Mend turned it into mourning), learning the hearth-song badly in front of Tabitha so that she hears what her daughter has been fed on, and asking Pim before anyone proposes a clause. Power buys only four to five minutes of held passage and is used last, to keep the Throat exactly as it is while Pim crawls through. Everyone keeps the right to refuse: Yeshe says yes only by action at the tide, the Second Hearth withdraws, Tabitha's pledge is voluntary, Pim chose. Costs kept: Pim misses the song, the Second Hearth turns its guest bench away, Tabitha must learn to let her daughter's arm go into a wall. Felt moment for Illuminara: astonishment at the end, and the care taken with Pim's name in the song. Fallback self-close (independent_peer_review false) because GPT wrote no S3 event after T01. The final has the real positive result attributable to Illuminara (Pim home, the Third Hearth keeps its guest and name, a seasonal Knock practice begins) with honest costs (the Second Hearth's turned bench, the promise only as certain as the seam, Yeshe's moved bowl). Turn is not power: the ending follows from the reading of ha-ru, the reciprocal gifts and Tabitha's own condition; the hold only keeps the Throat open. Remaining weakness, not a blocker: length well above the 1,500-2,500 guide.

final_critic_line: A child's one word, read as a promise to return, lets two houses that counted the same knock for generations finally answer it with a hand on a back, a jar of seed and a shelf kept.
